title: Merchants of Doubt: How a Handful of Scientists Obscured the Truth on Issues from Tobacco Smoke to Global Warming
author: Naomi Oreskes
Erik M. Conway
target_audience: General readers interested in science communication and environmental issues
Students and scholars of history, science, policy, or media studies
Professionals in public health, climate policy, or science advocacy
Journalists and media specialists covering scientific controversies
core_themes: Manipulation of public opinion and scientific uncertainty
Role of scientific authority and credibility in public discourse
Political and economic influences on science communication
Parallels between denial campaigns on tobacco, acid rain, ozone depletion, and climate change
The consequences of manufactured doubt for public policy and societal well-being
primary_purpose: To expose and document how a small group of prominent scientists, often with political and industrial ties, deliberately sowed doubt and confusion about the dangers of tobacco, acid rain, the ozone hole, and ultimately climate change, thereby influencing public perceptions and delaying effective policy action.

structure_format.narrative_style: Investigative, scholarly yet accessible, and narrative-driven
structure_format.organization: Chronological and thematic, divided into chapters each centering on distinct controversies and key individuals
features: Profiles of key scientists and institutions

key_concepts_lessons: Scientific uncertainty can be weaponized by vested interests to delay regulation and policy.
A relatively small group of scientists, leveraging their credentials, played influential roles in multiple denial campaigns.
Techniques honed in the tobacco industry were reused in later public health and environmental debates.
The media’s practice of ‘balanced’ reporting can unintentionally amplify fringe viewpoints and mislead the public.
Effective science denial relies on undermining scientific consensus and eroding public trust in expertise.
Manufactured doubt has far-reaching consequences for health, environment, and democracy.
notable_features: Draws direct connections across decades and different controversies
Relies on deep archival research and original documentation
Unmasks the recurring individuals and networks behind denial efforts
Explains complex scientific issues in an accessible way
cultural_historical_context: Published amidst growing debate and politicization of climate science in the late 2000s. The book situates the modern climate denial movement within a historical continuum of industry-funded doubt, aligning broader trends in American political and corporate strategies to contest regulation through the manipulation of scientific uncertainty.
reception_impact: Widely acclaimed for its rigor and readability
Influential in media, activist, and academic circles for clarifying the roots of climate denial
Adapted into a documentary film in 2014
Praised for exposing the networks and tactics behind anti-science campaigns
Cited frequently in discussions about science literacy and public policy
comparable_titles: The Doubt Machine: The Public Relations Industry’s Role in Climate Denial by the Center for Public Integrity
The Climate War by Eric Pooley
The Republican War on Science by Chris Mooney
